The bench, the story

For 35 years the same hands have kept the same standard: fewer pairs, more care, and a relationship built pair by pair. When Greenwich Shoe Repair moved from the storefront to a private practice, the goal was simple — serve clients who value craft over convenience, and give every shoe the time it deserves.

Questions from the bench

The answers George gives every day at the counter — tap a question to read it.

When do I need to protect my soles?

When they are brand new, when you first buy them, put on ‘sole guards’, as soon as it is possible.

When do you replace the rubber lift on elegant stiletto, low/high rise, shoes?

As soon as you see metal exposed through the rubber heel. Do NOT continue to wear them — it will cost more to repair than to drill out the nail.

Why should I keep my shoes, boots, & sneakers cleaned, waterproofed, & polished?

Polished shoes and boots, and waterproofed and cleaned sneakers, will prolong the life of the leather and fabric, protecting them against dirt, rain, sleet and snow, acting as a repellant. And, importantly, you look presentable on the job, on an interview, on the tennis court, and on the horse!

Water stains?

Water stains should be cleaned immediately by the shoe cobbler before they dry to avoid residue stain marks. If wet stain marks are left to dry, it is too late. Water and stain protectors or covering on shoes should be applied before, not after, wetness.

What is and when are shoes ‘dry-rotted’?

Dry rot is when material (rubber) deteriorates from normal heat/cold conditions and not being worn. Shoes can NOT be salvaged — shoes need to be replaced. Dry rot cannot be fixed! Buy some new ones!

What should be done to protect wearing high or low heel shoes on grass or gravel, outside for parties and outdoor events?

To protect and preserve, you must put on ‘clear plastic’ heel protective covers at the cobbler.

Can you repair all leather products like equestrian boots, tack, saddles, crops, golf bags and shoes, pocket books, jackets, luggage, etc.?

YES, most all leather goods, except dry-rot. If it is custom work, it requires custom pricing — it is the customer's responsibility to ask for pricing!

When can I expect my order to be completed?

You ought to receive a phone call from GSR that your order is done and ready for pick-up. If not, then please call GSR to confirm when it will be available at (203) 869-2288.
